profile.entities: Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL); Khavda RE park (group SPVs); Chitravathi PSP (Andhra Pradesh); offtaker/counterparty Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL)
profile.mgmt: Ashish Khanna (CEO); Rajat Seksaria (CEO — Battery Storage); Saurabh Shah (CFO); Vijil Jain (Head IR). Moderator: Baiju Joshi, Macquarie Capital
profile.subseg: Greenfield solar & wind; hybrid; battery energy storage (BESS); pumped-hydro storage (PSP)

deepdive.sec: Renewable Power Generation IPP (utility-scale solar/wind/hybrid + grid-scale storage)

bull_bear.body:
- The AESL contracting transfers merchant-tariff, ISTS/ALMM-waiver and market ups/downs (incl. the ~INR 0.50/unit transmission-cost arbitrage) **to AESL**; AGEL keeps predictable long-term returns.
- Continued reinvestment into greenfield + storage; no dividend/buyback (growth-stage IPP).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Transmission/evacuation availability** is the explicit growth governor.
- **Related-party concentration:** near-all merchant/C&I offtake now with sibling AESL (arm's-length/Audit-Committee-approved, but material RPT optics).
- BESS execution at 10 GWh scale unproven; battery-fire risk — mgmt clarified a competitor's incident was a **PCS/IGBT (inverter) fire, not a battery fire**; projects carry standard insurance + Tier-1 OEMs.
- Falling solar tariffs (units +30% vs revenue +29% roughly matched this quarter) — realisation compression on newer vintages.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and leadership-framed; CEO Ashish Khanna fielded most questions and articulated the de-risking rationale clearly. Some specifics deflected ("benchmark rate" rather than exact per-kWh AESL pricing). Battery-storage CEO Rajat Seksaria credible on fire/insurance and unit economics.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Business-model pivot:** from a merchant-tariff/transmission-arbitrage builder to a fixed-return contracted IPP via AESL — materially lower risk, lower upside, cleaner cash flows. The ISTS/ALMM-waiver and INR 0.50/unit transmission arbitrage upside now sits with AESL.
- The read-through of "grid, not panels, is the bottleneck" points straight at **transmission capex (AESL)** as the group's actual growth governor.
- AGEL ≈ India's entire grid-battery base today; first-mover scale advantage but also concentration risk.
- PSP (ex-Chitravathi) is still ~2 years out — storage growth near-term is BESS-led.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **AESL offtake structure:** solar/wind 25-yr fixed price (benchmark ~INR 2.7 / 3.4–3.5 per kWh), battery 15-yr fixed price, each project 25-yr arm's-length PPA on SECI standard terms, no termination-for-convenience; targets AGEL's ~15–16% hurdle IRR. Pricing set at market benchmark via Audit Committee (both listed entities).
- **BESS economics:** arbitrage model — charge ~INR 2.5, discharge INR 4–5 (INR ~4–5 spread) in evening peak; capex ~INR 1.5 cr/MWh; first 3.5 GWh contract fully capitalised by May-end. AGEL to start reporting BESS separately going forward.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Scale/execution moat:** AGEL is "virtually half of the total operational as well as battery-storage capacity in this country," heading to **more than two-thirds by year-end** — single-handedly defining India's grid-storage base.
- **Cost leadership:** 94% EBITDA margin on power supply; Khavda experience "phenomenally good," giving confidence to execute the next set of very large sites.
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.body:
| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "More transmission lines … come up" needed; evacuation is the growth bottleneck | **ADANIENSOL · 539254** — Adani Energy Solutions (grid/transmission + now the RE offtaker) ✅ | RE IPPs whose generation is stranded without lines | Grid-capex + 25-yr offtake pull; **High** — mgmt explicitly throttled adds to evacuation and routed all merchant/C&I to AESL |
| India's firming/storage gap for round-the-clock RE | **ADANIGREEN · 541450** (self — BESS 3.5→10+ GWh, PSP 500 MW) ✅ | Peaker/thermal flexibility providers as BESS scales | First-mover scale ≈ India's entire BESS base; **Med-High** |
| Curtailment (~5–7% EBITDA drag) until lines ready | **ADANIENSOL · 539254** (evacuation build-out) ✅ | ADANIGREEN near-term (curtailed MUs) | Resolves as transmission lands by CY26-end; **Med** |

latest_quarter.body:
- 94% power-supply EBITDA margin. Curtailment 5–7% EBITDA drag today, expected to fade by CY26-end.
- BESS: capex INR 1.5 cr/MWh, EBITDA INR 25–30 lakh/MWh; economics improve as more assets capitalise over the next nine months.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1FY27 (this):** Revenue from power supply INR 4,280 cr (+29%), EBITDA INR 4,122 cr (+33%, 94% margin), energy 13.7 BU (+30%); 20 GW crossed; capex INR 8,800 cr (+41%). **Strategic pivot:** all merchant/C&I contracted to AESL (25-yr solar/wind, 15-yr battery, fixed price, ~15–16% IRR). BESS 3.5 GWh installed (+1.9 GWh), targeting 10+ GWh this year, 50 GWh by FY30. Chitravathi 500 MW PSP on track this FY. FY27 capex ~INR 42,000 cr; run-rate EBITDA ~INR 17,000 → 21,000 cr. 7 GW transmission by end CY26. Curtailment 5–7% EBITDA drag, expected to fade by CY26-end.
- _next → check: 5 GW RE add vs plan; BESS progress to 10+ GWh; Chitravathi 500 MW commissioning; capex vs INR 42,000 cr; run-rate EBITDA to INR 21,000 cr; whether curtailment actually fades at Khavda; first separate BESS reporting; AESL pricing/RPT disclosures._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** no explicit revenue guidance; run-rate EBITDA to rise from ~INR 17,000 cr to **~INR 21,000 cr by FY27-end**.
- **Margin:** 94% power-supply EBITDA margin sustained; BESS EBITDA thumb-rule **INR 25–30 lakh per MWh**.
- **Capacity add FY27: 5 GW** greenfield solar/wind/hybrid (explicitly **excludes** BESS and PSP).
- **BESS: 10+ GWh** cumulative this fiscal (from 3.5 GWh); **50 GWh by FY30** ambition.
- **PSP:** maiden **500 MW Chitravathi (AP)** to commission this financial year; 5 GW PSP target by 2030.
- **Capex FY27: ~INR 42,000 cr.**
- **Transmission/evacuation:** additional **7 GW by end CY2026**; balance of ~14 GW pipeline over the following quarter or two.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- 20+ GW operational; Khavda (world's largest RE installation) >10 GW group solar/wind/hybrid operational.
- ~14 GW of evacuation capacity additions pending grid readiness (7 GW by end CY26).
- Virtually all merchant/C&I capacity now contracted to AESL; only direct-to-DISCOM (SECI-type) and temporarily-ahead-of-PPA infirm power sold by AGEL directly.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Storage is the second engine:** BESS 3.5 → 10 GWh this year → 50 GWh by FY30; PSP entering via Chitravathi 500 MW.
- Evaluating other **Khavda-scale greenfield sites** (high-radiation locations) on the back of Khavda execution confidence.
- Rising AI/data-center power demand and RE+storage firming cited as structural tailwinds.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Q1FY27 opened strong (power-supply revenue +29%, EBITDA +33% at a 94% margin, energy sales +30%, 20 GW milestone crossed), but the defining change this quarter is strategic: AGEL is **de-risking its merchant/C&I exposure by contracting essentially all such capacity to sibling Adani Energy Solutions (AESL)** on 25-yr (solar/wind) and 15-yr (battery) fixed-price arm's-length PPAs. AGEL reframes itself as a pure execution/operational-excellence play chasing predictable ~15–16% IRRs, while BESS scales fast (3.5 GWh installed, 10+ GWh targeted this year).

verdicts.note: 'we are currently planning to add 4.5 to 5.0 gigawatt of our solar and wind capacity' — FY27 ~5 GW guidance reaffirmed (slightly softened), not yet delivered. [±10% rule]
